content.text: mucocutaneous: oral acyclovir, valacyclovir or famciclovir; herpes labialis alt: topical penciclovir or docosanol; recurrent or severe labialis: famciclovir 1500 mg as 1 dose or valacyclovir 2 g PO every 12 h for 1 day; genital herpes (primary and recurrent): oral acyclovir, valacyclovir or famciclovir, most effective if started w.in 1 day of lesion onset; early tx of a primary infection doesn't prevent recurrences; pregnancy w genital herpes: acyclovir from 36 wks gestation ↓ recurrence and the need for C-section; immunocompromised, CNS infections or neonatal herpes: IV acyclovir; encephalitis: IV acyclovir for 14 to 21 days (prevents relapse).

acyclovir AEs: phlebitis, renal dysfun, rarely neurotoxicity (lethargy, confusion, seizures, coma; USU w renal insuff); acyclovir-resistant strains are also resistant to penciclovir, famciclovir and valacyclovir; foscarnet may be effective.

cold sores: 2 g twice daily for 1 day, 12 h apart, at the earliest Sx; initial genital herpes: 1 g twice daily for 10 days; recurrent: 500 mg twice daily for 3 days; suppression: 1 g once daily (500 mg once daily if ≤ 9 recurrences/yr). CI: hypersensitivity to valacyclovir, acyclovir or any component. TTP/HUS (some fatal) at 8 g/day in advanced HIV and transplant pts: stop at once if it occurs. Acute renal failure: elderly, renal dz on doses too high for renal funct, nephrotoxic drugs or poor hydration; caution in elderly and ↓ dose in renal impairment. CNS AEs (agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures, encephalopathy), more likely in elderly: stop if they occur.
